To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the expansion of outgoing geodesics in spherically symmetric collapse of a perfect fluid is a function only of the equation of state, (ii) this function has an asymptotic limit as the expansion approaches the central singularity, and (iii) this limit is independent of the equation of states.

(1) the expansion of null geodesics at the apparent horizon of a spherical dust collapse diverges in the approach to formation of a covered singularity, (2) the expansion of outgoing geodesics in the vicinity of the central world line of a spherical dust cloud diverges in the collapse to a covered singularity.
the expansion of outgoing geodesics is negative in the approach to the formation of a covered singularity, and that the expansion is positive in the approach to a naked singularity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the stability of the solutions of the Einstein equations in the context of spherical dust collapse.
the stability of singularity formation in spherical gravitational collapse.
the stability of naked singularity formation in the spherically symmetric gravitational collapse of matter with an equation of state that is not necessarily that of a dust fluid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the naked singularity formation in spherical dust collapse is a generic feature of the model.
the formation of a naked singularity is a stable phenomenon in spherical gravitational collapse of a general class of matter.
the naked singularity solution is not only stable but it also represents the most general solution of the spherical collapse equations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the spherical dust collapse the expansion is negative and the limiting value is finite and positive, which implies that the singularity is covered by the event horizon and that the singularity formation is a stable process in the sense that a small change in the equation of star will not change the nature of the solution.

the null geodesic focusing in the approach to the naked singularity is the same as that of a covered singularity and hence, the naked singularity does not focus the null geodesics to the extent that the singularity is hidden behind an event horizon.
the null geodesics expansion in spherical dust collapse is a monotonic function of the affine parameter and it approaches a limiting value as the affine parameter approaches infinity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expansion of outgoing radial null geodesics diverges at the moment of formation of a covered singularity and vanishes at the moment of the formation of a naked singularity, irrespective of the form of the matter content.
the null geodesic expansion is a useful probe to understand the nature of the singularity in gravitational collapse.
the expansion of outgoing geodesics in the vicinity of the singularity is determined solely by the matter density and the geometry of the collapsing cloud.
